name_note: GTDB's Hungatella effluvii also contains genomes that NCBI labels Hungatella hathewayi or Hungatella hominis, so some published work on H. hathewayi concerns genomes placed here.

sentences.text: Hungatella effluvii was described for strain UB-B.2, a Gram-stain-positive, spore-forming, strictly anaerobic rod isolated from an industrial effluent anaerobic digester sample.
The same work reclassified Clostridium hathewayi as Hungatella hathewayi, the type species of the new genus, and reported acetate and propionate as glucose fermentation end products of strain UB-B.2.
A case report described bacteraemia due to Hungatella effluvii in a man with chronic kidney disease, noting that such infections in humans are rare.
Its accompanying literature review suggested that Hungatella species infections may be associated with severe diseases such as sepsis and necrotizing fasciitis.
For the related Hungatella hathewayi, a study reported significant enrichment in faecal samples from colorectal cancer patients compared with healthy controls.
